issue.title: SEGV due to `ncurses` allowing sizes to be excessively large

labels.name: extension-modules
labels.description: C modules in the Modules dir

labels.name: type-crash
labels.description: A hard crash of the interpreter, possibly with a core dump

issue.body:
# Crash report

### What happened?

```python
import sys
import unittest
import curses

class TestCurses(unittest.TestCase):

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        stdout_fd = sys.__stdout__.fileno()
        curses.setupterm(fd=stdout_fd)

    def setUp(self):
        self.stdscr = curses.initscr()

    def test_refresh_control(self):
        stdscr = self.stdscr
        stdscr.refresh()
        win = stdscr.subwin(10, 15, 2147483647, 5)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
```

comments.body:
> ```SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: SEGV (/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libncursesw.so.6+0x19740) (BuildId: 84ef32c373c2b5b3c25dc788a1bcbbd3750cf9d1) in derwin```

The issue appears to be in the third-party library, I presume we don't sanitise the input (`2147483647`), and it is causing an overflow?
I think it's easy enough for us to add input sanitization in the meantime. We've done similar before in #122469 and #124555.

Changing it to short would definitely be a fix but actually, it's not the only function that would need this treatment and changing it everywhere to short seems a bad maintenance. Alternatively, we could have a type for "dimensions" for ncurses which would be short for now.

So, after looking at the code, I think it'd be too much work for validating this input on our side. It's better that this is validate in ncurses. The rationale is that some functions may or may not require memory allocation, or some functions may require allocation depending on the values. For instance, I don't know why `2147483647` doesn't work. It's `2^31 - 1` which fits on an `int` so there is no overflow here. Maybe that value is then used internally for something else, which then causes an overflow.
